_comment: Passive talents that modify the EQ spell pack (tools/eq_spell_pack.json). Consumed by tools/build_client_patch.py alongside the spell pack. Two kinds of talent: (1) 'mods' - a single-rank talent_dbc chain (IDs 90001+, above real Talent.dbc's max of 2285) whose rank is a passive spell (994001+) carrying up to 3 native SpellMod aura effects (SPELL_AURA_ADD_PCT_MODIFIER=108 / ADD_FLAT_MODIFIER=107), targeted at exactly one EQ spell via SpellFamilyName=220 + a classmask bit matching that spell's `family_bit` in eq_spell_pack.json (verified against SpellInfo.cpp's IsAffected() and SpellAuraEffects.cpp's IsAffectedOnSpell()). 'op' is the raw SPELLMOD_* enum from src/server/game/Spells/SpellDefines.h. IMPORTANT, verified the hard way: only a subset of SpellModOps actually apply to a fresh, one-off cast (checked every ApplySpellMod() call site in Spell.cpp/Unit.cpp/Player.cpp) - DURATION(1), RANGE(5), CASTING_TIME(10), COOLDOWN(11), DAMAGE(0)/DOT(22) [also covers periodic HEAL], COST(14) work. SPELLMOD_EFFECT1/2/3(3/12/23) do NOT work despite existing in the enum - AuraEffect::ApplySpellMod (SpellAuraEffects.cpp:813) only recalculates an aura that is ALREADY passive/permanent on the caster, which none of our one-off casts are - so a non-damage/heal aura magnitude (a slow %, a stat bonus, a resource-regen amount) has no generic modifier path on a fresh cast. Several base spells gained a DORMANT effect slot (EffectBasePoints -1, i.e. true zero, but a real SCHOOL_DAMAGE/PERIODIC_DAMAGE/PERIODIC_HEAL effect type) so a flat DAMAGE/DOT modifier can activate it. (2) 'pet_buff' - for the Cavorting Bones skeleton (a permanent SPELL_EFFECT_SUMMON_PET, not a temp Guardian - see the spell's own entry and the C++ patch in src/SpellDraft.cpp's OnPlayerBeforeGuardianInitStatsForLevel forcing PetType::SUMMON_PET for any owner class). The talent's passive spell here is a SPELL_AURA_DUMMY marker (required shape - SpellMgr.cpp's spell_pet_auras loader rejects anything else); `spell_pet_auras` (spell, effectId, pet, aura) then makes the engine natively cast `pet_buff.buff_spell_id` directly onto the matching pet (Unit::AddPetAura/CastPetAura, SpellAuraEffects.cpp:5176) whenever the owner has the marker - reactively, even on an already-summoned pet, and removed again on respec. The buff spell itself uses plain stat/damage auras (not SpellMod - a Pet is never target->IsPlayer(), so SpellModifier registration flatly does not apply to it). Talents are NOT added to LOCKED_TALENTS - purchasable with ordinary Talent Points. Avatar (pure Strength/Agility/Attack Power stat effects, no damage/heal effect, already using all 3 of its effect slots) has no non-duration lever available under the 'mods' constraints and so gets exactly one talent instead of four - flagged to the user rather than silently faked.
